KOLKATA: The Indian women’s hockey team’s Asian Games gold medal after a 44-year wait has done more than secure direct qualification for the Olympics.According to coaches who have nurtured generations of players across the country, the triumph has rekindled belief at the grassroots, and is destined to inspire a new generation of girls to take up the sport while validating decades of hard work in academies and training centres, far from the spotlight.Former India captain Pritam Siwach, who has been working as a coach for more than 25 years in Sonipat, Haryana, believes the impact of the victory extends well beyond the podium.“This victory has given women’s hockey a new lease of life. It is like giving water to a thirsty person. Winning gold after 44 years has ended a long drought and brought renewed energy to the sport,” she said, adding that the success has given women’s hockey the recognition it deserves after years of operating in the shadow of the men’s game.For coaches working at the grassroots level, the medal has become a powerful tool. Dasrath Mahato, the 69-year-old from Khunti in Jharkhand who discovered and mentored Nikki Pradhan, said every major success creates a ripple effect among young athletes.“When children see players returning home with medals, they start to believe they can do the same. It inspires them to work harder and pursue hockey seriously,” Mahato said.The success has also been celebrated by coaches who have worked in some of the country’s leading hockey centres. Madhya Pradesh Hockey Academy coach Vandana says achievements at the elite level invariably strengthen the grassroots ecosystem.“When a sport performs well at the top level, it benefits the grassroots. We are already seeing more academies and leagues being established for women, and success like this will only accelerate that growth,” said Vandana, who trained the likes of Sushila Chanu and Bichu Devi Kharibam.Former India goalkeeper and coach Edgar Mascarenhas, who worked extensively in Odisha, described the achievement as one of the biggest milestones in the history of Indian women’s hockey.“I watched every match and what impressed me most was their fighting spirit. Even in difficult situations, they never gave up,” said Mascarenhas.The direct Olympic qualification has also been highlighted as one of the competition’s biggest outcomes. Coaches unanimously agreed that avoiding the pressure of an additional qualification campaign allows the team to focus entirely on preparation for the Games.“This may actually be even more important than the gold medal itself,” said Siwach. “Now the players know they are going to the Olympics and can devote all their energy towards preparing for that challenge.”The impact has been felt in regions that have emerged as strong contributors to Indian women’s hockey. In Mizoram, where coach Miss Btei helped nurture internationals Lalremsiami and Lalthantluangi, interest in the sport continues to grow among young children.“The success of players from our state will encourage more youngsters to take up hockey. Children see what Lalremsiami has achieved and begin to believe they can follow the same path,” she said.According to Btei, players as young as nine or ten years old, are now entering the development pathway with the latest generation already benefiting from the visibility created by the national team’s success.For former India international and coach Ajit Lakra, the gold medal represents proof that India’s grassroots structures are delivering results.“These players came through the grassroots system and delivered a gold-medal performance that resonated across Asia. It shows young athletes that there is a pathway from the grassroots level to the international stage,” said Lakra, who coached Rutuja Dadaso Pisal.While they welcomed the growing number of opportunities for women, the coaches stressed the importance of greater investment in infrastructure, academies and player development programmes to sustain the momentum.Yet the overriding sentiment remains one of optimism. Whether in hockey strongholds like Jharkhand and Odisha, established academies in Madhya Pradesh or emerging centres like Mizoram, coaches see the medal as a catalyst for growth.
Article Summary: The Indian women's hockey team's Asian Games gold medal after a 44-year wait has done more than secure direct qualification for the Olympics. The triumph has rekindled belief at the grassroots, and is destined to inspire a new generation of girls to take up the sport.

Article Title: The road to LA 2028: How Sjoerd Marijne and his team rebuilt India's women's hockey side
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, tears flowed freely on the pitch. More than 5,500km away, in India, women’s hockey’s loyal legion, small in numbers but deep in investment, rejoiced.They had watched a team in which skill was matched by fitness, individual brilliance was backed by teamwork and, finally, belief had returned.The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics was unprecedented.Interest in women’s hockey had gathered pace after India’s fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics. Missing out on Paris, however, dented the hopes and aspirations that had begun to build.Then came the well-documented rifts, allegations, a dip in form and a spate of injuries. The shadow over Los Angeles grew darker.Enter Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff. They did not have a magic wand to make the demons disappear. What they brought was a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.The Dutchman was quick to point out that rebuilding a team is never the work of one person.“There’s a great connection among the staff and the players. I’m doing the interviews, but it’s an achievement from the whole staff. I’m really happy with all the quality I have around me,” he said.But there was another requirement, ensuring the players were fit enough to play as one.That was where Wayne Lombard, the team’s head of athletic performance, came in. He had a broad idea of the physical state of the squad when he arrived.The support staff hit the reset button. Rodet Yila and Caira Yila were brought in as scientific advisers, while the immediate priority was not fitness for fitness’ sake, but getting the players healthy.“Regardless of what the fitness levels were, the priority was to address the injury concerns,” Lombard said.That required more than exercises and numbers. The players had to believe in the process.“We had to sit down with the players and earn their buy-in. Helping them understand that the physical side of the game is every bit as important as the technical and tactical side,” Lombard said.He introduced the 30-15 intermittent fitness test to establish the players’ maximum aerobic speed. The test required them to run for 30 seconds, rest for 15 and progress across a 40m grid, with the speed increasing by 0.5kmph at every stage.Muscle by muscle, the players rebuilt their strength. With it came confidence.As the year progressed, India began to look increasingly like a team t rather than a collection of talented individuals.Poetic justice or coincidence, Japan had stood in India’s way in the qualifiers for the Paris Olympics. In Japan, a little over two years later, India cleared the hurdle to Los Angeles.
Article Summary: The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics was unprecedented. Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff brought a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.

NAGOYA: It has been a testing three weeks for Japan. Article Title: New beginnings, new heroes: Women lead India's charge as a new generation shines in Nagoya
Article Text:
Lovlina Borgohain and Neeru Dhanda (Image credit: X)

The comeback girls

Golden standards

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As Neeru Dhanda led the Indian contingent out for one last time at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday night, it was symbolic of how India’s Asian Games campaign had unfolded over the past two weeks.The women had come to the fore - packing punches, vaulting to new heights, lifting weights, taking aim, towering over opponents with sixes, blazing the track, finding the fairway and hitting the back of the net. India’s final tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, may represent a drop from the 106 medals and 28 golds won in Hangzhou. But numbers alone cannot tell the story of these Games.There were path-breakers everywhere, athletes who pushed through glass ceilings that had stood for years. The aftermath will bring reviews, reflections, deliberations and reports. But before the analysis begins, it is only fair to celebrate those who made these Games count.For almost 12 days, the Indian gold rush had remained subdued. Then, just as the sun finally began showing up in Nagoya, the floodgates opened. Eleven gold medals came in the final two days, transforming what had threatened to become a disappointing campaign into a collection of stories about guts, resilience and glory.Dhanda, the 26-year-old from Sangatpura in Haryana, had set the tone by winning India’s first individual gold of these Games in the women’s trap event. The women went on to win 11 gold medals, apart from the three secured in mixed events.The contingent had 83 debutants, who accounted for 41 of India’s 85 medals — a clear indication of a changing guard across several sports.But if one athlete were to be picked as the face of that change, it would be difficult to look beyond 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod. The Maharashtra archer won two gold medals and a silver, but her biggest achievement went beyond the medal tally.She ended South Korea’s two-decade domination of the women’s recurve events by becoming the first Indian to win individual recurve gold at the Asian Games. It did not take her long to make the biggest stage of her young career her own.Even her Korean opponent Oh Ye-jin, whom Kumkum beat for the individual gold, was left impressed. “For a 17-year-old, she is very composed and has a very bright future,” Oh said.Another teenager, Prithika Pradeep, also emerged with two gold medals, adding to the sense that a new generation is beginning to announce itself. Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf gold.Behind every medal was a story of humble beginnings, survival in sport, societal pressures overcome and personal tragedies endured. That made the successes more than just entries in a medal table.They were not newcomers to the big stage. They had competed at the biggest of them all — the Olympics. But Nagoya offered unfinished business.Lovlina Borgohain had contemplated walking away from boxing after a difficult phase post the 2024 Paris Olympics. Instead, she returned to punch her way to gold.Parveen Hooda, returning after a doping ban, produced her own golden comeback. The bronze she had won in Hangzhou and subsequently lost became gold in Nagoya. Mirabai Chanu did not win gold, but her silver in the 49kg category had the weight of a champion’s achievement. It also completed her Asian Games medal collection.The women’s kabaddi team survived a tense battle against Iran. The women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold. And Harmanpreet Kaur and her team ensured that cricket’s gold returned to India.Among the men, too, there were performances that demanded attention — Aman Sehrawat in wrestling, Ankush Panghal in boxing and Gulveer Singh in long-distance running among them.Yet, for all the celebration, there were glaring blanks. Manu Bhaker, one of India’s biggest sporting heroes, returned without a medal.There were plenty of nearmisses and some disastrous outings. India’s badminton return of a solitary bronze was another disappointment, particularly with a strong men’s doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen in the squad.Table tennis also raised questions, while equestrian had its own share of run-ins between administrators and riders, alongside selectionrelated concerns but failed to add to the medal count.
Article Summary: India's final tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, may represent a drop from the 106 medals and 28 golds won in Hangzhou. But numbers alone cannot tell the story of these Games. There were path-breakers everywhere, athletes who pushed through glass ceilings that had stood for years.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: PM Modi congratulates Team India, hails ‘determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit’
Article Text:
Indian contingent at the Asian Games closing ceremony and PM Narendra Modi

‘Immense joy to the nation’

Historic golds and landmark performances

Looking beyond Aichi-Nagoya

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday congratulated the Indian contingent for its performance at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games , praising the athletes for representing the country with “determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit” as India concluded its campaign with 85 medals.India finished fourth on the medal table with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, ending the Games with its second-highest medal haul in Asian Games history. The tally was 21 medals fewer than the record 106 won at the Hangzhou edition in 2023.As the Games drew to a close in Nagoya on Sunday, Modi took to X to applaud the entire contingent and the medal winners while also expressing hope that the performances would help strengthen Indian sport at the grassroots level.In his post, the Prime Minister praised the athletes for their effort and sporting spirit throughout the continental showpiece.“As the Asian Games 2026 draw to a close, my compliments to every member of the Indian contingent for representing our nation with determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit. Congratulations to all our medal winners, whose performances have brought immense joy to the nation.May these Games inspire even greater achievements in the years ahead. May they contribute to strengthening sports at the grassroots too,” Modi wrote.The Prime Minister’s message came after more than two weeks of competition involving athletes from 45 countries. The Aichi-Nagoya Games witnessed a string of record-breaking performances, including 54 world records.The Games formally concluded with a spectacular closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya on Sunday.India’s campaign was marked by several historic performances and successful title defences across disciplines.Both Indian cricket squads retained their Asian Games titles, while the men’s and women’s kabaddi sides also won gold. The men’s hockey side successfully defended its title with a 5-1 victory over Malaysia, while the women’s team ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final.There were also several breakthrough individual performances.Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold, while 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod created history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold at the continental showpiece.Mohod was also part of India’s historic women’s recurve team gold that ended South Korea’s seven-edition winning streak in the event. Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal, meanwhile, produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of the Games to win the men’s 65kg freestyle gold.Boxer Lovlina Borgohain also joined an elite group of Indian women by becoming only the second after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold.Athletics emerged as India’s biggest medal contributor with 24 medals, while shooting accounted for 15. Archery was the most successful sport in terms of gold medals, producing five top finishes.The campaign also provided a series of important milestones ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, with several young athletes making their mark on the continental stage.Earlier, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha named Mohod and Kalkal the inaugural recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively for the best female and male Indian sportspersons of the Games.With the Aichi-Nagoya campaign now complete, Modi’s message placed the emphasis not only on India’s medal tally but also on the broader legacy of the Games — inspiring another generation of athletes and strengthening the sporting ecosystem from the grassroots upwards.
Article Summary: India finished fourth on the medal table with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. The tally was 21 medals fewer than the record 106 won at the Hangzhou edition in 2023. Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the athletes for their effort and sporting spirit throughout the continental showpiece.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: PT Usha names Kumkum Mohod, Sujeet Kalkal as Team India’s MVPs after historic golds
Article Text:
Kumkum Mohod and Sujeet Kalkal

Mohod ends South Korea’s long reign

India's Kumkum Anil Mohod (Image: REUTERS)

Kalkal turns a lost final into gold

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sujeet Kalkal with coach after winning gold medal. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: Teenage archer Kumkum Mohod and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal have been recognised as the standout performers of India’s campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, with Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha naming them the inaugural recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively.The two awards have been instituted by the IOA to honour the best female and male sportspersons of the Games and commemorate the legacy of two stalwarts of Indian sport.Seventeen-year-old Mohod, making her Asian Games debut, won three medals, including two golds, while 23-year-old Kalkal produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of the Games to claim gold in the men’s 65kg freestyle wrestling category.India finished fourth in the medal standings with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.Mohod was at the heart of one of the biggest breakthroughs for Indian archery in Aichi-Nagoya.Along with Ankita Bhakat and Kirti, she won the women’s recurve team gold, ending South Korea’s remarkable run of seven consecutive Asian Games titles in the event dating back to the 1998 Bangkok Games.Mohod then followed it with gold in the individual recurve event, ensuring that South Korea’s women failed to win a recurve gold at the Asian Games for the first time in the discipline’s history.Her individual triumph also secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Usha praised Mohod’s ability to deliver under pressure and drew a parallel with the late Jaspal Rana, after whom the award has been named.“It is fitting that Kumkum is the first recipient of the Jaspal Rana Award, as Jaspal too burst onto the scene as a prodigy at the 1994 Asian Games. Her composure under pressure and her ability to find her best form when her back was to the wall augur extremely well for Indian Archery,” Usha said.The IOA president believes Mohod’s breakthrough could finally help Indian archery cross a long-standing barrier at the Olympics.“India's archers have been knocking on the door for more than a decade now, and I firmly believe that this performance by Kumkum and her recurve teammates has shattered the glass ceiling for Indian archery. India came close to winning a maiden Olympic medal in the sport at the Paris Olympics, and I am convinced that the final frontier will be breached at the Los Angeles Olympics,” Usha added.Kalkal, meanwhile, earned the Raja Randhir Singh Award after a gold-medal run that showcased his resilience and fighting spirit.The 23-year-old defeated reigning Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semifinal before producing a stunning comeback against Abdulmazhid Kudiyev in the final.Kalkal trailed 2-9 with time running out but refused to give up, fighting back to win 10-9 in a dramatic finish. His triumph also continued India’s strong tradition in the 65kg category, following Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, who won Asian Games gold in the same weight class in 2014 and 2018 respectively.Usha said it was Kalkal’s refusal to accept defeat that made his performance particularly special.“Wrestling is India's sport, and Sujeet's performance will be spoken of for years to come. The gold medal will be celebrated, but his never-say-die attitude and refusal to accept silver have earned him a special place in the hearts of all Indians,” she said.“Winning gold medals in elite competition is not easy, but equally important is the effort that goes in when your back is against the wall. I wish Sujeet all success in the years ahead and will be rooting for him to deliver India's first-ever wrestling gold medal at the Olympic Games in two years' time.”The IOA will felicitate Mohod and Kalkal at a ceremony in the coming days.Their selection provides a fitting individual recognition to two athletes whose performances stood out in India’s 85-medal campaign.
Article Summary: Kumkum Mohod and Sujeet Kalkal recognised as standout performers of India’s campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Teenage archer Mohod won three medals, including two golds, while 23-year-old KALKal produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of the Games. The two awards have been instituted by the IOA to honour the best female and male sportspersons.

Article Title: Asian Games: Leaner Indian contingent produces fewer golds but better return-per-medal - in numbers
Article Text:
Gold medallist India's players during the medal ceremony for the men's hockey event. (PTI Photo)

Where did the golds go?

Shooting, athletics behind the decline

Late surge takes India to 85 medals and fourth spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The overall medal gap never disappeared

In late August, the Sports Ministry maintained that the qualification criteria for the Asian Games, put into place a year ago, would not change despite criticism. “The idea, from the very beginning, was to send a lean contingent. The criteria was announced a year ago, and everyone had the time to figure it out and qualify,” a Sports Ministry source told TimesofIndia.com back then. It was made clear that the objective was to have a contingent with only realistic medal contenders making the trip to Aichi-Nagoya."Let’s take an example. If somebody has to run inside 10 seconds to be a contender for a medal in the 100m event, should we send an athlete who clocks 15 seconds? We have set the criteria that if an athlete is in the top six in Asia, we will select him or her, otherwise not. We have followed that,” the source had said.The tennis squad went from 12 to 7. Several judokas and wushu athletes were removed from the initial list. From 44 players in 2022, no footballers were sent this time. There was also no place for 20 hoopers and 16 handball players.India had sent a 661-athlete contingent to the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. Three years later, the final contingent that travelled to Japan was trimmed to 495 athletes.After 14 days of competition, India accounted for 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes for a combined 85 medals. For comparison, India had won 106 medals in China (28 golds, 38 silvers, and 40 bronze).As the contingent size dropped by 25.1%, the golds fell by nearly the same number (25%) and medals by 19.8%. India won 16 medals for every 100 athletes in Hangzhou. In Aichi-Nagoya, that figure rose to 17.2% — an improvement of about 7.3%.Stripped to the bare bones, India won 0.172 medals per athlete in Nagoya, against 0.160 in Hangzhou. Golds per athlete were essentially unchanged at about 0.042. Crudely, it counts every athlete sent, including those who did not medal. At the same time, teams as big as cricket (30 athletes), hockey (40) and kabaddi (24) account for a single medal in a discipline.So while India did not match its record 106-medal haul, its smaller contingent produced a slightly better medal return per athlete.The more complicated part of the comparison comes when gold medals are brought into the mix.India's gold medal tally fell from 28 to 21, a 25% decline — exactly in line with the reduction in the size of the contingent. The gold-medal yield was therefore virtually unchanged: 4.24 golds per 100 athletes in Hangzhou and 4.24 in Aichi-Nagoya.That suggests the smaller contingent was not, by itself, the reason India's gold tally fell. Rather, the composition of the medal haul changed.India's 2022 golds came heavily from three sports: shooting (seven), athletics (six), and archery (five), which is 18 of 28 (64%). In Nagoya, archery again delivered five, but shooting produced three and athletics one. Boxing, which won no gold in Hangzhou, won three, and wrestling won two after none. Golf added a gold courtesy Pranavi Urs. Squash, which won two golds in 2022, won none, despite the expectations from Anahat Singh, though the overall count of five medals did not change.The team sports carried more of the load. Cricket, hockey and kabaddi won six of India's 21 golds, up from five of 28. India completed a double title finish in all three. In 2022, hockey had produced one gold and one bronze.Athletics' podium shifted down a step. In 2022, it returned six golds, 14 silvers and nine bronzes. Now, despite a massive 75-plus-member contingent, it produced one gold, nine silvers and 14 bronzes.Shooting (4) and athletics (5) were the biggest reasons behind the drop in gold medals. Squash (2), Badminton (1), Tennis (1) and Equestrian (1) all also witnessed a drop in the yellow metal. Tennis, in fact, didn't produce a medal at all - a first in 40 years.In Hangzhou, shooting and athletics were the two biggest contributors to India's gold medal tally, producing seven and six gold medals, respectively. Together, they accounted for 13 of India's 28 golds. In Aichi-Nagoya, that combined figure collapsed to four. Shooting contributed three golds, while athletics produced one. India therefore lost nine gold medals from these two sports alone.The sub-par show from the athletes was made murkier by the withdrawals of 100m hurdler Jyothi Yarraji and triple jumper Praveen Chithravel. Both national record holders had skipped the Indian Athletics Series Final in prelude to the Asian Games, citing knee stress and a calf muscle pull, respectively.When it came to the Asian Games, Yarraji pulled out of the women's 100m hurdles first-round heats after "feeling pain" during the warm-up under rainy conditions.Chithravel, meanwhile, attempted his first jump but could not complete it, exiting the competition area clutching his calf in apparent pain. He was later taken away in a wheelchair. Men's 400m hurdler Yashas P., too, pulled out after starting his Heat.Coming to the shooters.India's 2026 shooting tally of 15 medals (3 golds, 8 silvers and 4 bronzes) was a 32% drop in total medal tally when compared to 22 in the previous continental showpiece. The gold haul took a 57% hit. Broken further, seven were team medals, five individual and three in mixed team events.The gold medals came in one individual (Neeru Dhanda in women's trap) and two mixed team events (Neeru and Kynan Chenai in mixed trap and Suruchi Phogat and Kamaljeet in mixed 10m air pistol).If the final medal tally tells one story, the daily trajectory tells another. Through the first 12 days of competition, India had won 10 gold medals in Aichi-Nagoya. In Hangzhou, India had already accumulated 21 golds by the same point.Then came the late surge in Japan.India won 11 gold medals over the final two days of its 2026 campaign — six on Day 13 and five on Day 14. That means 52.4% of India's entire gold haul came in the final two days. The equivalent figure in Hangzhou was 25%: seven of India's 28 golds came during the final two days.India had 13 golds by Day 8 in Hangzhou. At the same stage in Aichi-Nagoya, it had four. By Day 11, the gap was still eight golds — 18 to 10.But the final stretch changed the picture dramatically. India collected 18 golds across Days 13 and 14 in the two editions combined, but the distribution was very different: seven in Hangzhou and 11 in Aichi-Nagoya.On October 2, the women's recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod picked a gold. As did boxer Lovlina Borgohain on her birthday. Parveen Hooda also joined the party alongside wrestler Sujeet Kalkal's remarkable comeback, boxer Ankush Panghal's drought-ending gold, and the women's hockey team's triumph over China to seal an LA 2028 spot.A day later, archer Kumkum Mohod, golfer Pranavi Urs, wrestler Aman Sehrawat, the men's cricket team, and the men's hockey team gave the country plenty to celebrate with golden flourishes.The same late surge was visible in the total medal count, but it was not enough to close the gap with Hangzhou.After the first day, India had five medals in Hangzhou and two in Aichi-Nagoya.By Day 4, the difference had grown to 10 medals.By Day 8, it was 16.By Day 11, Hangzhou's cumulative tally stood at 80 medals, compared with 60 in Aichi-Nagoya — a 20-medal gap.India narrowed that deficit slightly over the next two days, reaching 76 medals against Hangzhou's 94 after Day 13.But the final day added nine medals in Aichi-Nagoya and 12 in Hangzhou, leaving the final difference to 21.
Article Summary: India had sent a 661-athlete contingent to the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. Three years later, the final contingent that travelled to Japan was trimmed to 495 athletes. India accounted for 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes for a combined 85 medals. For comparison, India had won 106 medals in China.

Article Title: ‘Learn from these Games and keep moving forward’: Abhinav Bindra’s message to Team India as LA Olympics beckons
Article Text:
Indian athletes leave the arena following the closing ceremony for the Asian Games in Nagoya. (AP Photo)

'Enormous respect to our athletes'

'LA is less than two years away'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Olympic gold medallist Abhinav Bindra has urged Indian athletes to learn from both the successes and disappointments of the Asian Games 2026, calling for stronger high-performance systems and a renewed focus on preparations for the Los Angeles Olympics, which are less than two years away.Congratulating India's athletes and support teams after the country finished fourth in the Aichi-Nagoya Games with 85 medals, Bindra highlighted the years of hard work and sacrifices behind their performances while stressing the need for an honest assessment of the campaign.India finished with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, falling short of its record haul of 106 medals at Hangzhou 2023. However, the campaign produced several historic achievements, including gold-medal sweeps in men's and women's cricket, kabaddi and hockey.In a lengthy post on X on Sunday, Bindra thanked athletes, their families, coaches and support staff for their contributions before urging the sporting establishment to turn the lessons from Aichi-Nagoya into meaningful improvements."Congratulations to every Indian athlete and to Team India on the Asian Games. A Games campaign is never just the few days we see on television. It is years of early mornings, injuries, doubts, missed occasions and countless hours of work," Bindra wrote."So first and foremost, enormous respect to our athletes and also to their families who live this journey with them and make sacrifices that are rarely seen. To the coaches, support staff, federations, SAI, the Government and everyone working behind the scenes, THANK YOU!"The 2008 Beijing Olympics gold medallist in shooting acknowledged the breakthrough performances in Aichi-Nagoya, particularly those of young athletes who announced themselves on the continental stage. However, he stressed that disappointments must also be examined rather than simply forgotten."There have been some terrific breakthrough performances at these Games. Young athletes have announced themselves, others have stepped up to a new level, and there have been moments that give us a lot to be excited about. There have also been disappointments. That is sport, and every Games will have them. What matters now is how honestly we learn from them," he added.Bindra called for a more comprehensive approach to athlete development, arguing that high-performance programmes must provide the right expertise throughout an athlete's career rather than stepping in only when medals are within reach."High performance cannot only be about reacting when an athlete is close to a medal. We have to keep building systems that understand the athlete over several years," he wrote.He emphasised the importance of sports science, data-driven decisions, coaching, competition planning, training-load management, recovery and injury prevention, alongside building physical and mental resilience."Most importantly, the right expertise has to reach the athlete at the right stage of their career, not when it is already too late," he said.With the next Summer Olympics approaching, Bindra warned that the preparation window was shrinking and called for immediate action."LA is less than two years away. In Olympic sport, that is not a long time. The athletes who will stand on the podium there are already deep into their preparation today."His message was to celebrate the achievements, acknowledge shortcomings and return to work with renewed determination."Be proud of what has been achieved. Learn from these Games and keep moving forward. Wishing Team India everything good on the road to LA," he concluded.
Article Summary: Bindra urges Indian athletes to learn from successes and disappointments of the Asian Games 2026. Olympic gold medallist calls for stronger high-performance systems and a renewed focus on preparations for the Los Angeles Olympics. India finished with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, falling short of its record haul of 106 medals at Hangzhou 2023.

Article Title: From 1-1 to 1-6: India’s challenge to Uruguay ends in a harsh reality check
Article Text:
Uruguay's Darwin Nunez, 9, celebrates with teammates after scoring a penalty during an International friendly Football match between India and Uruguay, in Kolkata. (PTI Photo)

Kolkata:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For a brief period on Tuesday, the Salt Lake Stadium became a cathedral of dreams for Indian football.The sky was gloomy and grumpy, threatening to open up at any moment. But as the clock ticked 22 minutes, Ryan Williams, almost unnoticed, began his run from the centre line like someone feeding on his inner brute.Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur was left searching for answers in his wake as India’s No. 10 continued with pace and potency before unleashing a piledriver from the edge of the box. Uruguay goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo managed to parry it partially, but Anirudh Thapa followed with all his predatory instinct to snap up the rebound.Everything about the goal was so delightfully done — the thrill of it, the kill of it.Suddenly, there was life after India had conceded an 11th-minute goal through a Darwin Nunez penalty. It was 1-1 against two-time World Cup winners and a team currently ranked No. 20 in the FIFA rankings. And suddenly, Khalid Jamil’s India made their football look bold and beautiful.Then lightning struck, literally, forcing the players to leave the field. The game was suspended for a mandatory 30 minutes.When the two teams resumed the contest, Uruguay flipped the narrative with a class-topper’s swagger.Maximiliano Araujo made it 2-1 for Diego Forlan’s team going into the break.After the changeover, Forlan’s team came out with a vengeance. Araujo got his second in the 59th minute, while further goals from Rodrigo Zalazar (53), Juan Manuel Sanabria (71) and Rodrigo Sebastian Aguirre (86) completed Uruguay’s eventual 6-1 demolition of India.Amid all the fight and frustration, it was the kind of performance from Jamil’s side that was infused with a sense of hope, despite being India’s heaviest defeat at this ground, eclipsing Thailand’s 5-0 dismantling of the home side in the 1995 Nehru Cup.Through Edmund Lalrindika’s movements inside the box, Williams’ incisive run and those thunderous strikes from second-half substitutes Mohammed Sanan and Sahal Abdul Samad that forced timely interventions from the Uruguayan goalkeeper, India tried to seize their moment and showed a new way of looking the big boys in the eye.Adopting a high line against Nunez and Araujo was also a statement of intent.In such an exhibition of admirable belief, there were moments which clashed and coalesced in equal measure, but India always tried to measure up to the excessive demands of such games against World Cup regulars.It was perhaps this new India’s bold approach that forced Forlan to think differently about his game plan when play was suspended.The essence of Uruguayan football identity is rooted in ‘garra charrua’ — a dogged, street-savvy idea of rising to the challenge against all odds.After the World Cup debacle, Forlan has inherited a team which no longer thrives in this ‘garra charrua’ spirit, as reports of dressing-room mutiny and players’ defiance of his predecessor Marcelo Bielsa’s training methods marked a tense, disorderly end to the Argentine’s tenure as Uruguay coach.Whether a game against India would inspire much urgency in this respect is debatable, but it should give him an interesting window into the change in mentality in Indian football, with Forlan returning here 10 years after his Indian Super League days as a Mumbai City player.
Article Summary: Uruguay beat India 6-1 in an international friendly in Kolkata. Darwin Nunez, Maximiliano Araujo, Rodrigo Zalazar, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Sebastian Aguirre scored for Uruguay.

Article Title: Who is Anirudh Thapa? The Indian footballer who ended 44-year wait for a goal against two-time World Cup champions Uruguay
Article Text:
Anirudh Thapa ended India’s 44-year wait for a goal against Uruguay, joining Manas Bhattacharya as only the second scorer/ Image: X

Anirudh Thapa ends India's 44-year wait against Uruguay

Manas Bhattacharya was the first Indian to score against Uruguay

Who is Anirudh Thapa?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: India's Anirudh Thapa, left, celebrates with Ryan Williams after scoring a goal during an International friendly Football match between India and Uruguay, in Kolkata. (PTI Photo/Manvender Vashist Lav)(PTI10_06_2026_000500B)

India may have suffered a heavy 6–1 defeat to Uruguay in Kolkata, but one moment still gave the home crowd something significant to celebrate. Anirudh Thapa's equaliser against the two-time FIFA World Cup champions ended a 44-year wait for an Indian goal against La Celeste, placing the midfielder alongside a player from a very different era of the national team's history.Thapa became only the second Indian footballer to score against Uruguay when he reacted quickest to a rebound and turned it into the equaliser during Tuesday's international friendly at the Salt Lake Stadium.Uruguay had taken the lead in the 11th minute after Indian defender Pramveer was penalised for a foul inside the area, with former Liverpool forward Darwin Núñez converting the resulting penalty after sending Gurpreet Singh Sandhu the wrong way.India responded just 11 minutes later, with Ryan Williams winning possession in midfield before carrying the ball forward and striking from the edge of the box.Uruguay goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo managed to parry Williams' effort, but Thapa had followed the move closely and reacted first to the loose ball before calmly finishing from the rebound.The goal briefly brought India level at 1–1 and gave the home side a huge lift against a Uruguay team ranked 20th in the world, with India sitting 138th.It was also an important personal moment for Thapa, because the strike was his fifth international goal and his first for India since March 2023.Uruguay eventually pulled away in the second half, with Maximiliano Araújo scoring twice while Rodrigo Zalazar, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Aguirre also found the net to complete a 6–1 victory.Thapa's goal nevertheless secured his place in a very small piece of Indian football history.Before Thapa's rebound at the Salt Lake Stadium, the previous Indian goal against Uruguay had been scored 44 years earlier by Manas Bhattacharya.Bhattacharya found the net during the 1982 Nehru Cup at Eden Gardens in Kolkata, although his goal could not prevent India from losing the match 3–1.Uruguay had already built a two-goal advantage through Jorge da Silva before Bhattacharya pulled one back in the 35th minute.The goal made Bhattacharya the first Indian to score against Uruguay, a distinction he held for more than four decades before Thapa joined him on Tuesday night.Bhattacharya was a prominent winger during the 1970s and 1980s and earned a strong reputation during his spells with Mohun Bagan and Mohammedan Sporting.India and Uruguay have only met twice previously, with Uruguay winning both encounters, although the second meeting came against a Uruguay B team during the 2001 Millennium Super Soccer Cup in Kochi.That match ended 3–0 to Uruguay, meaning Thapa's strike was the first Indian goal against the South Americans since Bhattacharya's effort in Kolkata in 1982.Thapa was born in Dehra Dun on January 15, 1998, and the 28-year-old has become one of the more established midfielders in Indian football after several years around the national-team setup.He currently plays for Mohun Bagan Super Giant in the Indian Super League and has already won the ISL twice during his career, while making his senior India debut in 2017 and accumulating more than 60 international appearances.His development began when he started playing football at the age of 10 with St. Stephen's Football Academy in Chandigarh.Thapa then represented India's under-14 side before earning a place at the AIFF Regional Academy in Kalyani in 2012, later moving into the AIFF Elite Academy and eventually captaining the I-League under-19 team.In 2016, he was one of four Indian players selected for an opportunity with French Ligue 2 club Metz, giving him an early taste of European football before he established himself domestically.His Indian Super League journey began in 2016 when Chennaiyin FC signed him, followed by a loan move to Minerva Punjab after the 2018 ISL season.Thapa made his debut for Minerva Punjab against Mohun Bagan in January 2017 before returning to Chennaiyin in May that year when his loan spell ended.After the 2021–22 ISL season, Thapa left Chennaiyin and joined Mohun Bagan, where he continued developing as one of India's established midfield options.His goal against Uruguay now gives that career another notable chapter, because despite India's eventual 6–1 defeat, Thapa has become only the second Indian player ever to find the net against the two-time world champions.
Article Summary: Anirudh Thapa scored India's equaliser against Uruguay in Kolkata. The 28-year- old's goal ended India's 44-year wait for a goal against La Celeste. Thapa became only the second Indian to score against Uruguay. Manas Bhattacharya was the first Indian to do so in 1982. India suffered a 6-1 defeat to Uruguay in the international friendly.

Article Title: ‘We would not be marking Messi’: Benin defender’s heartwarming message ahead of Argentina icon’s farewell
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi trains for his final game with the national team. (AP Photo)

Messi’s final bow for Argentina

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A farewell to remember

Benin defender Mohamed Tijani has offered a heartwarming perspective ahead of Lionel Messi’s final international appearance for Argentina, saying his team will not man-mark the legendary forward but instead savour the opportunity to share the pitch with one of football’s greatest icons.Argentina face Benin in a friendly at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, with the match set to mark Messi’s farewell in the famous blue-and-white shirt. The occasion has been billed as an emotional celebration of the 39-year-old’s extraordinary international career, with thousands of fans expected to turn out to bid farewell to their captain.Speaking to Argentine outlet C5N ahead of the game, Tijani made it clear that stopping Messi would not be the only priority for Benin.“We would not be marking Messi. We will just enjoy this match. I will watch him and say: Messi, you are a legend,” Tijani said, as quoted by Goal.com.The Benin defender’s admiration for Messi goes even further. According to Goal.com, Tijani said he hoped Argentina would win the farewell match, despite his own side being the opposition.“We will do our utmost to ensure this celebration is perfect,” Tijani said, speaking about Messi’s final international outing.Messi announced his decision to retire from international football on September 1, following Argentina’s 0-1 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. He had previously retired from international duty in 2016 after Argentina lost the Copa America final to Chile, but reversed that decision and subsequently enjoyed the most successful period of his international career.Messi led Argentina to Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024 before finally achieving his long-held dream of winning the World Cup in Qatar in 2022. Argentina defeated France on penalties in the final after a thrilling 3-3 draw.His farewell comes after a record-breaking international career. Messi is Argentina’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player, having made 207 appearances and scored 125 goals for his country. He has also scored 21 goals across six World Cup appearances.Messi’s final international appearance is expected to be an emotional occasion at the Monumental, where more than 85,000 supporters are set to witness the Argentine great take the field for one last time for his country.The Argentine Football Association has described the occasion as one that will “transcend sports” and be filled with emotion. Messi himself reflected on the significance of the moment after joining up with the Argentina squad for the final time.“Special moments I know I will miss,” Messi wrote on social media.While his international career is coming to an end, Messi will continue playing club football for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.
Article Summary: Argentina face Benin in a friendly at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday. Lionel Messi is set to make his final appearance for his country. Benin defender Mohamed Tijani says his team will not man-mark Messi. The 39-year-old announced his retirement from international football on September 1.

Soccer Football - International Friendly - India vs Uruguay - Salt Lake Stadium, Kolkata, India - October 6, 2026 Uruguay's Rodrigo Aguirre celebrates scoring their sixth goal with teammates REUTERS/Sahiba Chawdhary

TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: India's third and final friendly test on home soil ended on a losing note as they went down 1-6 to Uruguay at the Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday. Anirudh Thapa's first half strike gave the home faithful something to celebrate in what was a heartening performance in the first half despite the scoreline. A Brace from Maxi Araujo coupled with goals from Rodrigo Zalazar, Darwin Nunez, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Aguirre put the game beyond India.India held Panama to a 1-1 draw in Bengaluru in the first friendly of the FIFA international window. They were then swept aside 0-4 by Brazil on Saturday in Kolkata. The six goals conceded on Tuesday, in front of 37,307 fans, dampened what had been a promising start to the three important friendlies.In a game that witnessed a lightning strike enforced 30-minute delay, Uruguay were far and above the better side in the second half to nullify India's solid first half showcase.The promising start quickly unravelled as Uruguay capitalised on defensive lapses and moments of transition to secure a comprehensive win, their second of the tour of Asia, having earlier beaten South Korea.India, meanwhile, had their moments, particularly in the opening stages, but Uruguay’s greater quality in the final third eventually told.The visitors repeatedly exposed gaps behind the Indian defence, with Maxi Araujo and Zalazar among those making the most of the opportunities presented to them.India had the first meaningful opening in the fifth minute when Akash Mishra met a corner inside the box and attempted a left-footed strike, but his effort sailed over.Edmund Lalrindika was then presented with an even better opportunity after India won possession high up the pitch. The ball fell to him with only the goalkeeper to beat, but he lacked composure and drifted wide before running out of room.Uruguay were awarded a penalty soon after, with Pramveer adjudged to have brought down Federico Viñas inside the box. The decision was greeted with loud boos from the home crowd, who felt the Uruguay forward had gone down too easily. Darwin Nuñez made no mistake from the spot, sending Gurpreet Singh Sandhu the wrong way to give Uruguay the lead.The visitors almost doubled their advantage in the 16th minute. Nunez was sent through and, rather than shoot, cut the ball back for M. Araujo, whose curling effort beat Gurpreet but came back off the post.India responded impressively and were level in the 22nd minute.Ryan Williams found himself with plenty of space and, encouraged by the crowd, unleashed a shot that goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo could only spill. Anirudh Thapa reacted quickest, staying onside before producing a composed left-footed finish to make it 1-1.India continued to threaten, with Williams again involved minutes later. He drove forward on the right and found Edmund in the centre, but after a couple of touches inside the box, the Indian forward was crowded out by the Uruguay defence.The momentum was then interrupted by a thunderstorm. Play was stopped at 8:04pm, with players and staff sent back to the dressing rooms. After a 30-minute delay, as per FIFA's protocols revolving lightning, the match resumed.Uruguay needed just two minutes after the restart to regain the lead.A cross from the right by Nandez caught India off guard. Ashique Kuruniyan attempted to step up, but the space he left allowed Nandez to exploit the opening, with Araujo finishing the move to put Uruguay 2-1 ahead.India were increasingly vulnerable on the counter. Nunez was played through by Zalazar in the 37th minute and found himself completely clear, but his attempted chip was thwarted by Gurpreet, who stood tall and managed to get his body behind the effort.After the half time break, Uruguay took complete control of the game.Zalazar extended the lead in the 53rd minute after Nunez nodded the ball down into his path on the edge of the box. Zalazar took a touch before unleashing a powerful strike into the bottom corner, giving Gurpreet no chance.Araujo added his second of the night six minutes later. Viñas slipped a through ball behind the Indian defence and Araujo raced beyond the backline, shrugging off Abhishek Singh before calmly finishing past Gurpreet for 4-1.India continued to look for a response. Gurpreet denied Zalazar at one end, while Apuia tried his luck from distance at the other, only to see his effort sail over.Sanan briefly lifted the home crowd in the 69th minute, weaving past one defender before creating space for a long-range attempt. His lofted effort was punched over by the goalkeeper, prompting a huge roar from the stands.But Uruguay immediately exposed India at the other end.Another transition caught the hosts out and Sanabria finished at the far post to make it 5-1.The visitors added a sixth late on. Facundo Pellistri burst down the right before finding Aguirre in space on the edge of the box. Aguirre took a touch, wrong-footed Bijoy and curled a superb finish into the top corner, leaving substitute goalie Albino Gomes with no chance.Uruguay's 6-1 victory ultimately reflected the gulf between the sides in terms of ruthlessness and the ability to punish mistakes. India showed enough attacking intent to suggest there were positives to take, but their defensive organisation was repeatedly exposed whenever Uruguay accelerated the game.
Article Summary: India lost 1-6 to Uruguay at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata on Tuesday. Anirudh Thapa's first half strike gave the home faithful something to celebrate. A Brace from Maxi Araujo coupled with goals from Rodrigo Zalazar, Darwin Nunez, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Aguirre put the game beyond India.

Article Title: Why Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina are blocked from Messi’s farewell despite whole 2022 World Cup-winning squad being invited
Article Text:
Roma have blocked Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina from attending Lionel Messi’s final Argentina farewell due to scheduling and travel concerns/ Image: Instagram

Roma block Dybala and Molina from travelling to Argentina

Gasperini explains why the timing was impossible

Why Dybala and Molina were not with Argentina anyway

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lionel Messi's final Argentina appearance was supposed to bring together almost the entire group that helped him win the 2022 World Cup, but two familiar faces will be missing from the occasion. Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina were both invited to attend the farewell with their families, yet their return to Argentina will have to wait after Roma decided the timing was simply too difficult for the club.AFA president Claudio Tapia invited every member of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad to attend Messi's farewell against Benin, with the players and their families expected to be part of the celebrations at the Estadio Monumental.Dybala and Molina have now become the first two confirmed absences from that group, after Roma refused to release the pair for the transatlantic trip despite neither player being involved with Argentina during the current international window.Roma explained their decision in a statement issued on Tuesday, pointing to the length of the journey and the proximity of the club's next competitive commitments.“AS Roma announces that Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina will not participate in the event organized in Argentina for the match between Argentina and Benin on October 6,” the statement said.“The club recognizes the importance of this appointment for the two players, who are linked to Lionel Messi and played a key role in his victory at the 2022 World Cup. The club's choice was based on sporting and logistical reasons, linked to the length of the intercontinental trip and the proximity of official commitments.”“AS Roma expresses its utmost respect for Lionel Messi and his extraordinary career, wishing him and the Argentine Federation a special evening.”Roma currently lead Serie A after five matches, level on points with reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio, which has made the club particularly reluctant to lose important players for a ceremonial trip at this stage of the season.Roma head coach Gian Piero Gasperini also addressed the decision before Messi's farewell, making the issue sound much more practical than personal.Roma's first match after the international break comes away to Como 1907 on October 11, only five days after Messi's final Argentina appearance, while a major meeting with Real Madrid follows soon afterwards.Speaking to Sky Sport Italia on Monday, Gasperini explained why he did not want Dybala and Molina making the long journey to South America before returning directly into a demanding domestic schedule.“We are too close to an important game like our one on Sunday [to let Dybala and Molina fly to and from Argentina],” Gasperini said. “We’re a long way from Argentina and sending them there would have meant making them fly for a lot of hours so close to the match and Roma preferred for that not to happen.”Despite blocking the trip, Gasperini made clear that he understood what the occasion means for Messi and those who played alongside him during Argentina's greatest period of recent success.“Messi’s farewell will be emotional,” Gasperini said. “Personally, I’ve seen lots of star players, initially as a player myself and then as a coach, but it’s hard to think of anyone who’s achieved what Lionel has. I’m sorry to see his career with the Albiceleste come to an end.”Had Lionel Scaloni selected Dybala and Molina for Argentina's September-October international window, Roma would have had little room to prevent either player from travelling for Messi's farewell.Their absence from the squad, however, comes for very different reasons.Dybala has not played for Argentina since making a brief appearance against Colombia during the 2026 World Cup qualifiers on September 10, 2024.Despite producing strong seasons in European football, Dybala has never established himself as a regular part of Scaloni's attacking plans, with his position overlapping with Messi and younger players such as Nico Paz and Franco Mastantuono now receiving opportunities ahead of him.Molina's situation is more straightforward, because he remains unavailable to Argentina while serving a seven-match suspension for his involvement in the clashes that followed the 2026 World Cup final.The pair have nevertheless remained closely linked to the generation that delivered Argentina's third World Cup star, with Dybala and Molina combining for 105 international appearances.While they will miss the chance to share Messi's farewell with their former World Cup teammates, several other Serie A-based players will attend, including Inter captain Lautaro Martínez, Juventus winger Nico González and Como forward Nico Paz.Roma will also have three players represented at the occasion through Argentina's squad, with Leonardo Balerdi, Matías Soulé and Santiago Castro included for the farewell match.
Article Summary: Roma block Dybala and Molina from travelling to Argentina for Lionel Messi's final appearance for the Albiceleste. AFA president Claudio Tapia invited every member of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad to attend Messi's farewell against Benin. Roma refused to release the pair for the transatlantic trip despite neither player being involved with Argentina during the current international window.

Article Title: 'Not here to be tourists in Argentina': Benin goalkeeper ahead of Lionel Messi's farewell match
Article Text:
Argentina footballer Lionel Messi

‘We are here to compete’

No free goal for Messi

NEW DELHI: Benin goalkeeper Marcel Dandjinou has made it clear that Argentina’s farewell celebration for Lionel Messi will not stop his team from competing. As Benin prepare to face Argentina at the Monumental, the 28-year-old goalkeeper says his focus will be on doing his job, even if that means denying Messi a goal on his final night.Dandjinou, who plays for Kruger United in South Africa’s Premier Division, spoke to Spanish newspaper Marca after arriving in Buenos Aires.Despite reports of problems with Benin’s preparations, including claims about poor hotel facilities and difficulties in training, he insisted the team had been treated well."We did not face any problems. We are fine here in Buenos Aires. Why do you say that? The truth is that we have had good conditions," he said.Dandjinou admitted that facing Messi makes the match particularly special, but stressed that Benin are not travelling to Argentina simply to watch the superstar."For me, this match is not like any other match. I think it is an opportunity that will not come again, because it is Messi's last match. It is a special match. But, look, we are here for Argentina and for Messi, but we must not forget that we represent our country too," he added."We are here to defend Benin. This is football: eleven players against eleven. We can win, or draw, or they can win, but it is football. We are not here to be tourists in Argentina; we are here to play and to compete. It will be a great day in our lives."The goalkeeper has huge respect for Messi, having grown up watching him play."For me, Messi is one of football's legends. We grew up watching him play. He is one of our favourite players. To be able to play against him now, on the same pitch, is incredible. I never imagined this would happen, but it will happen on Tuesday. For me, Leo is a legend, a true legend," he further remarked.Asked whether he would allow Messi to score a penalty in the final minutes as a farewell gesture, Dandjinou gave a firm answer."No, no. I am a goalkeeper, and my job is to save the ball. Even if it is the final minute and a penalty is awarded, if Messi takes it, I will try to save it. It is that simple: it is football. Yes, we are here to celebrate Messi, but no one has asked us to give him a goal. And knowing Messi, there is no need to give him anything. If he wants to score, he has to do his best to achieve it," he explained.While every Benin player would love Messi’s shirt, Dandjinou joked that the squad could need plenty of them."If you asked any player in my team, he would tell you he wants his shirt. So it would be great if they made a lot of shirts and gave one to each player. Because if only one of us goes to ask for the shirt, I do not think it will be easy: we all want one," he continued."It would be a great honour for me to play, and that memory will remain engraved in my mind forever. During my career I will be able to say: I was there, in the last match of a legend, in Messi's last match. It is incredible."On the eternal Messi-Cristiano Ronaldo debate, he concluded, "We grew up watching Messi and Cristiano. They taught us a lot about football. They have been competing for a long time. For me, Leo is one of the best players in this sport, indeed one of its kings."
Article Summary: Benin goalkeeper Marcel Dandjinou says his focus will be on doing his job, even if that means denying Messi a goal on his final night. Despite reports of problems with Benin’s preparations, including claims about poor hotel facilities and difficulties in training, he insisted the team had been treated well.
